title: Status Page Transparency Upgrades — Launch Checklist (Status Page v2)
content:
Purpose
This checklist is the practical, end-to-end launch gating doc for Status Page Transparency Upgrades ("Status Page v2") across: (1) component taxonomy + mapping, (2) incident comms templates + training, (3) automation (incident-bot + approval), and (4) monitoring + rollback.

Audience
- Launch captain: Console/Tooling (Nora)
- SRE launch approver: Rafael
- Observability approver: Allison / Aisha
- Support/CS readiness: Dev / Jasmine

Launch principles / constraints (reminder)
- Do not over-promise SLAs; status updates must be factual and reversible.
- Avoid customer-specific capacity disclosures (Dedicated/Private visibility rules apply).
- Reduce on-call burden: default templates + automation; no manual busywork under Sev1+.
- Prevent status flapping (hysteresis + anti-flap) and avoid "everything is down" when impact is scoped.

Scope of this launch
- New public component layout (product surface x region where applicable)
- New internal source-of-truth component registry + validation
- Health signal mapping + dashboards
- Incident-bot: intake fields, draft generation, publishing client, reminders, optional approval for Sev0/Sev1
- Training + enablement: IC / Comms Lead / Scribe workflow
- Console linking: linkouts to status incidents + post-incident summaries (phase dependent)

Out of scope (explicit)
- Changes to formal customer SLA documents
- Publishing root cause details that would compromise security or customer confidentiality

Phased rollout (target)
Phase 0 — Staging validation (internal only)
Phase 1 — Internal dogfood (Redwood staff uses new component taxonomy + automation; public page unchanged)
Phase 2 — Limited public rollout (subset of components enabled / rollout_flag)
Phase 3 — Full public rollout (all new components enabled + templates become default)

Owner map for launch gating
- Component taxonomy + registry: Christine / Ravi
- Signal mapping + anti-flap: Allison / Aisha
- Incident-bot + approval: Devon / Miles
- Runbook + templates: Rafael / Paula / Wei
- Support readiness + macros alignment: Dev
- Console linking / UI: Nora / Marissa

Pre-flight: prerequisites (must be done before any staging cut)
[ ] Confirm "source of truth" location for component registry and review process is in effect (ADR-014).
    - Owner: Christine
    - Notes: Registry changes require review by SRE + Observability. No direct edits in-prod without PR.

[ ] Confirm component taxonomy page is finalized and matches registry ids/display names.
    - Owner: Christine
    - Check: Display names are customer-friendly; ids are stable; regions are consistent (us-east, us-west, eu-west).

[ ] Confirm incident comms templates page is finalized (Investigating/Identified/Mitigating/Monitoring/Resolved) + tone rules.
    - Owner: Paula / Wei
    - Check: No promise language ("will be resolved by"). No RCA speculation.

[ ] Confirm Dedicated/Private incident visibility guidance is documented (what can/can’t be posted publicly).
    - Owner: Kira / Michael (Legal) / Naomi (Security)
    - Check: Dedicated control-plane signals may show availability without exposing tenant-level details.

[ ] Confirm status-page update runbook is updated and linked from alerts.
    - Owner: Rafael / Allison

Staging validation checklist (Phase 0)
Goal: prove correctness and usability in staging, including "bad days" (false positives, partial region issues, misclassification).

A. Config + schema validation
[ ] Component registry JSON schema validation passes in CI (no missing fields; ids unique).
    - Owner: Christine
    - Evidence: CI green on registry PR; version tagged.

[ ] Registry includes required metadata fields used by tooling (ownership, rollout_flag, grouping).
    - Owner: Christine

[ ] Mapping layer tests cover top 10 routes/capabilities (chat, streaming, embeddings, reranking) across primary regions.
    - Owner: Ravi / Logan
    - Notes: include "embeddings misclassified as chat" regression test.

B. Observability + signal correctness
[ ] Dashboards exist per public component (latency + error panels) and are accessible to on-call.
    - Owner: Aisha

[ ] Anti-flap logic is enabled and tuned in staging (hysteresis, minimum duration).
    - Owner: Allison
    - Test: simulate 2–3 transient spikes; verify status does NOT toggle.

[ ] Burn-rate / threshold annotations include runbook links and component_id labels.
    - Owner: Allison

C. Incident-bot workflow staging
[ ] Incident intake requires component + region + capability (or explicit "unknown" with follow-up reminder).
    - Owner: Devon

[ ] Draft generation produces correct template block per incident state (Investigating/Identified/Mitigating/Monitoring/Resolved).
    - Owner: Devon / Paula
    - Test: create a mock incident; ensure text is readable and doesn’t leak internals.

[ ] Statuspage API client uses idempotency keys + retry/backoff; audit log events recorded.
    - Owner: Devon

[ ] Optional approval step works for Sev0/Sev1 (Support lead or IC) without blocking urgent updates.
    - Owner: Devon / Dev Patel
    - Test: approval required only when publishing externally; drafts still generated immediately.

D. "Partial impact" scenarios
[ ] Confirm we can mark "Streaming (us-east)" degraded without impacting "Hosted API (us-east)" if only streaming is affected.
    - Owner: Rafael / Allison

[ ] Confirm we can represent latency-only degradations as "Degraded Performance" (criteria met) without marking outage.
    - Owner: Allison / Rafael

[ ] Confirm multi-region incident can be represented cleanly (two components vs one broad component) without confusing customers.
    - Owner: Nora / Paula

E. Runbook usability (dogfood exercise)
[ ] Run a 30-minute game-day in staging: IC + Comms Lead + Scribe.
    - Owners: Rafael (IC), Paula (Comms), Christine (Scribe)
    - Success criteria: first public-ready update drafted within 10 minutes; component selection correct on first attempt.

Go/No-Go for leaving staging
- All staging checks above completed.
- At least one simulated incident end-to-end (intake → draft → approval (if needed) → publish in staging).
- Observability dashboards + links verified by on-call engineer who was NOT involved in implementation.

Production readiness checklist (Phase 1/2/3)
A. Rollout configuration
[ ] Define rollout strategy (rollout_flag per component; default OFF for new components until enabled).
    - Owner: Christine / Nora

[ ] Confirm "legacy" component grouping remains available for rollback.
    - Owner: Nora
    - Note: keep old ids intact until after post-launch audit period.

[ ] Backfill plan approved (what historical data we will/won’t backfill) and timeline is documented.
    - Owner: Allison / Ethan

B. Component backfill (historical + current)
[ ] Verify component health widgets show "Operational" by default for all enabled components.
    - Owner: Allison

[ ] Backfill job executed in dry-run mode; validates it does not create retroactive incidents or customer confusion.
    - Owner: Allison / Christine

[ ] Backfill job executed for agreed time window (per plan) and results spot-checked.
    - Owner: Allison
    - Spot check: us-east streaming panels show correct baseline; embeddings panels reflect known incident days accurately.

C. Console integration (if included in current phase)
[ ] Console links to status incidents and post-incident summaries behave correctly.
    - Owner: Nora
    - Check: No customer-specific context is displayed unless explicitly allowed.

[ ] Accessibility + mobile layout sanity check (status page component list grouping).
    - Owner: Nora / Design (DES-244)

D. Comms training + enablement
[ ] Comms Lead rotation list published; expectations (TTFU targets, approval rules) reviewed.
    - Owner: Rafael / Paula

[ ] 2 training sessions held (one for SRE/on-call; one for Support/CS).
    - Owner: Paula / Dev Patel
    - Content: templates, what to say when unknown, how to update components, who approves Sev0/Sev1.

[ ] Quick-reference doc pinned in #incidents and #support (link to templates + runbook).
    - Owner: Paula

[ ] Support macros updated to align with new status language (especially "Investigating" and "Monitoring").
    - Owner: Dev Patel

E. Monitoring and measurement plan (day-0/day-7)
[ ] Enable weekly status accuracy audit job and confirm it’s paging/creating a ticket (not waking on-call).
    - Owner: Allison

[ ] Confirm metrics dashboards exist for:
    - time-to-first-update (TTFU)
    - number of status corrections per incident
    - mismatches flagged by audit job
    - support ticket deflection (approx; qualitative OK initially)
    - Owner: Allison / Rafael

[ ] Define on-call "watch" for first 72 hours post public rollout:
    - who monitors
    - which signals
    - what constitutes rollback
    - Owner: Rafael

Launch execution steps (run of show)
Phase 1: Internal dogfood (recommended minimum 1 week)
[ ] Enable incident-bot new intake fields + draft generation for internal use.
[ ] Require components for all internal incidents (even if public update not posted).
[ ] Collect feedback: 5 on-call engineers + 2 Support reps.
[ ] Track issues: missing components, unclear template phrasing, too many prompts, approval friction.

Phase 2: Limited public rollout (subset)
[ ] Select initial public components for enablement (suggest: Hosted API (us-east/us-west/eu-west), Streaming (us-east), Embeddings (us-east)).
[ ] Confirm Support is aware of which components are live and how to interpret statuses.
[ ] Announce internally in #announcements: what changed + where to file issues.

Phase 3: Full public rollout
[ ] Enable remaining components per plan.
[ ] Switch templates to "default" in incident-bot for any status update action.
[ ] Verify status page layout grouping and naming in production.

Post-launch: audit + cleanup (first 2 weeks)
[ ] Run first accuracy audit and review results in SRE weekly.
    - Owner: Rafael / Allison

[ ] Identify top mismatch patterns and file follow-up tickets (instrumentation vs training vs mapping bugs).
    - Owner: Christine / Logan

[ ] Review Support tickets tagged "status accuracy" and summarize learnings.
    - Owner: Dev Patel

[ ] Decide when to deprecate legacy components (do not remove until mismatch rate is stable and customers have adjusted).
    - Owner: Sean / Neha (approval)

Rollback plan (must be pre-approved)
Trigger conditions (examples)
- Incorrect component mapping causes public misinformation in active incident (e.g., wrong product surface shows degraded)
- Flapping causes repeated component status toggles that increases customer confusion
- Status update publishing is blocked (approval deadlocks) during Sev0/Sev1

Rollback actions (ordered)
1) Disable rollout_flag for new components (revert to legacy component set).
2) Disable automation publishing step (incident-bot continues drafting; humans publish manually).
3) Revert registry/mapping config to last known-good tag.
4) If needed: temporarily reduce granularity (region split) for a subset while fixing signals.

Rollback owners + approvals
- Execution: SRE on-call IC
- Approval (if time allows): Rafael or Sean
- Support notification required: Dev Patel (or on-call Support lead)

Communication during rollback
- Internal: update #incidents and #support with what is changing and why.
- External: only if rollback impacted an active customer-visible incident update; keep short and factual ("We are adjusting the component display while we validate signal accuracy").

Open questions / decisions needed before public rollout
- Which components are included in Limited public rollout (Phase 2)? (Proposed list above; needs PM/SRE signoff.)
- Dedicated control-plane components: do we expose globally or per-region initially? (Need Kira + Security review.)
- What is the default behavior when region is unknown at incident start? (Allow "Unknown" with reminder vs block publish.)

Notes to self / gotchas (from prior incidents)
- Streaming can fail independently of non-streaming chat completion; ensure on-call doesn’t mark broad API outage by habit.
- Embeddings errors have been misclassified previously; always validate with component dashboards before publishing.
- Keep first update simple. It is better to be precise about uncertainty than to be verbose.

Last updated
2025-12-02 — Added rollback triggers, clarified Phase 2 suggested components, and added Support macros readiness item.
